To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CH2 and the CH3 domains of the Fcgamma1-CH2-CH3 fragment are in close contact with each other, that this contact is stabilized by the presence of a glycan tree structure on each of the CH2 domains and that the CH3 domains show a high flexibility.

molecular dynamics simulations of IgG1- Fc can help in the understanding of the cross-talk between the CH2 and the CH3 domains and that this information is valuable in the design of Fcabs, a new format of antibody fragments.

molecular dynamics simulations can be used to identify the structural regions of the IgG1-FC that are most prone to conformational changes and that these regions are also most likely to be involved in the design of new antigen binding Fc domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rational design approach for the generation of Fc-based binding proteins.
the structural stability and dynamics of the Fc region of the human immunoglobulin G1 and the impact of point mutations and glycosylation on the conformational dynamics of the protein.
the development of a computational approach for the design of Fc-based antigen binding proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hinge region and glycan tree structure are of importance for the stability of IgG1 Fc.
molecular dynamics simulations of IgG1 Fc can help to understand the impact of point mutations in the scaffold IgG-Fc on the overall protein structure.
IgG1 Fc is an interesting format for the design of antigen-binding Fc proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular dynamics simulations are in good agreement with experimental findings.
the CH3 domain is a very important domain for the stability of the Fc.
molecular dynamics simulations of IgG1 Fc can provide valuable insights into the structural and functional aspects of this scaffold protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
molecular dynamics simulations can help to better understand the structural and dynamic properties of IgG1 and its mutants.
the Fc scaffold can be engineered to generate a wide array of binding proteins.
the hinge region and CH3 domain are the most important factors in determining the stability of the IgG1 Fc fragment.
